title: Frugal Console surface: surgical MVP trim for dashboards, tracing, and cost-explorer
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: reduce the initial Console observability surface to ship a practical, high-value MVP within the quarter. This ticket documents specific scope cuts and the acceptance criteria that preserve core user flows for early customers while deferring higher-cost items (detailed trace waterfall, per-token cost breakdown, and per-route anomaly scoring) to later milestones.
background: Multiple roadmap reviews and telemetry cost estimates pushed the Console MVP past acceptable delivery risk. We need a minimal, supported set of dashboards and inspectors that provide actionable signals for teams integrating Redwood (latency hotspot detection, gross cost trends, and simple model route health) without the full fidelity tracing or per-token economics that drive long implementation time and high telemetry costs.
scope_changes: Keep: Route-level cost summary card (7d/30d) with delta vs baseline (aggregated, sampled)
Keep: Top-5 slow routes latency card with p50/p95 and acceptors for anomaly flagging
Keep: Error-rate trend and recent error log sampler (limited 100 rows) for first-touch debugging
Defer: Full span waterfall visualization (trace waterfall) to post-MVP - provide a lightweight span-link placeholder that deep-links to tracing platform
Defer: Per-token cost breakdown and token-attribution view - expose aggregate cost and per-route unit cost only
Remove for MVP: Real-time streaming trace timeline and full trace sampling controls
Remove for MVP: In-console route anomaly ML scoring (defer to telemetry-2) - replace with deterministic threshold rule alerts
Constrain: Dashboard card counts capped at 6 on initial release; card configuration is read-only until phase 2
Add: Developer-facing troubleshooting panel with prioritized quick-links (recent errors, top slow calls, last-deploy metadata) to reduce time-to-first-debug
acceptance_criteria: Console shows Route Cost Summary card that updates every 10 minutes and matches billing aggregation within 3% for a 24h window (sampled),
Top-5 Slow Routes card displays p50 and p95 latency and supports a single-day and seven-day view; p95 delta calculation must be documented
Error-rate trend card shows error rate by route and returns a max of 100 log rows when user expands; expanding log rows links to raw logs dashboard
Lightweight trace placeholder exists and deep-links to vendor tracing OR a documented support workflow if tracing not provisioned
All MVP cards load under 1.5s on 95th percentile for internal test accounts under nominal load
Telemetry cost for MVP (ingest+retention) must be <= projected budget line item 3 in the PRD (see linked cost model), otherwise scope must be further reduced
Design sign-off on visual density and legibility for each card (accessibility contrast pass),
Acceptance QA passes smoke flows: open console, view dashboard cards, follow deep-link to trace/log, validate cost delta number against sample billing job
decisions: Prefer aggregated, sampled metrics over full-fidelity traces to keep telemetry cost in check
Deferral: advanced ML anomaly scoring and token-level cost telemetry deferred to telemetry-2 roadmap
Ship read-only cards in MVP to reduce configuration surface and enable faster delivery; card editing to be implemented in a later cycle
Provide deep-link fallback for tracing so customers with existing tracing stacks retain triage capability
engineering_feedback: ENG: Runtime team recommends coarse-grained cost aggregation at route-group level to avoid expensive join operations on token attribution
ENG: Tracing team warns full span waterfall will add ~3.5x CPU cost under high ingest; deferral is aligned with infra constraints
ENG: Need a lightweight sampling strategy for error log sampler - proposed deterministic reservoir sampling implementation (spec in ENG-83421)
ENG: Suggested implementation plan: build cards with backend feature-flag gating to enable/disable additional fidelity post-launch
design_feedback: DES: Simplify card chrome and remove dense micro-interactions to keep accessibility high
DES: Provide a single CTA per card (view details / deep-link) to reduce cognitive load
DES: Use aggregated sparklines instead of full mini-heatmaps for MVP to reduce render complexity
DES: Accessibility: ensure color palette passes contrast 4.5:1 for status indicators
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP rollout): internal beta to 5 pilot customers (feature flag enabled) for 2 weeks
Collect telemetry on card load times, sampling error rates and sampling bias; run weekly review
Phase 2: enable read-only card customization and increase trace fidelity behind an opt-in flag
Rollback criteria: any production customer sees >10% error-rate increase linked to Console telemetry pipeline or card render latency exceeding 3s on 95th percentile
